exchanges.q: What did you do for work in {COUNTRY}?
exchanges.a: I had a small bakery in {TOWN}. I worked there with my son for eight years.
Members of the {GROUP}. They came to the bakery every Friday.

a: At first they asked for fifty dollars a week.
After six months they raised it to two hundred dollars a week, and I could not pay.

exchanges.q: What happened when you could not pay?
exchanges.a: In September 2020 they kidnapped my son for two days. They released him after I paid one thousand five hundred dollars.

exchanges.q: Did you go to the police?
exchanges.a: I went once, to the station in {TOWN}. The officer said he could not help me and told me to pay.

exchanges.q: Did the gang members ever hurt you physically?
exchanges.a: Not me. They broke the windows of the bakery, and they hit my son.

exchanges.q: Why didn't you move to another city?
exchanges.a: We moved to my sister's house in {CITY} for four months, but they found us there.

exchanges.q: How do you know it was the same group?
exchanges.a: I think so, because one of them was the same man who came to the bakery. He had a tattoo on his neck.

exchanges.q: Is there anything else you want the court to know?
exchanges.a: Only that my son is still afraid. He was seventeen years old when they took him.
